research_mode: official ONS, OSR and Police.uk sources only; current crime-statistics production and designation, 2025-2027 crime-data-integrity inspection design, IT and QA oversight, NDQIS and PND quality controls, and stop-search precision and missing-state contracts; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: 2025 to 2027 inspection coverage
verified_claims: each force is scheduled for crime-data-integrity inspection in the 2025 to 2027 PEEL round
inspection findings support quality interpretation
inspection timing is not continuous
limitations: coverage does not imply simultaneous observation
inspection evidence must be dated

sources.name: Current crime-data-integrity inspection design
verified_claims: forces no longer receive a graded crime-data-integrity judgment
HMICFRS uses a dip sample of files
relevant findings feed other PEEL core questions
limitations: dip samples are not full audits
absence of a grade is not evidence of perfect recording

sources.name: Escalation to full audit
verified_claims: concerns about crime recording can trigger a full crime-data-integrity audit
routine dip sampling and full audit are distinct
escalation is risk-based
limitations: no escalation does not certify every record
audit scope and date must be retained

sources.name: Crime data quality framework
verified_claims: the data quality framework rates offence trend reliability
ratings use good, moderate or poor classes
criteria differ for CSEW and police recorded crime
limitations: ratings are offence-level not parcel-level
classes should not be converted to numeric safety

sources.name: Offence-specific reliability examples
verified_claims: homicide trend reliability is rated good
knife or sharp instrument offence reliability is rated moderate
recommended source differs by offence
limitations: ratings concern trend reliability
they do not validate individual incidents

sources.name: OSR review evidence sample
verified_claims: the review engaged a sample of nine police forces
it also consulted HMICFRS Home Office ONS and wider stakeholders
OSR cautioned that findings may not generalise to all forces
limitations: sample evidence is not a census
review conclusions need scope metadata

sources.name: Crime-recording IT-system variation
verified_claims: seven different crime-recording IT systems were in use
some forces used different versions of the same system
system variation is a barrier to standardisation
limitations: system inventory can change
system identity alone does not quantify record error

sources.name: IT migration data-quality risk
verified_claims: crime-recording system changes can harm data quality
changes can disrupt data sent to the Home Office
supplier dependence can delay or increase the cost of fixes
limitations: risk differs by force and supplier
not every migration causes an error

sources.name: Force-level quality-assurance variation
verified_claims: internal audit stages were broadly similar
record checking and validation standards varied
operational priorities resources and IT systems shape QA arrangements
limitations: broad similarity does not prove equivalent assurance
force-specific evidence is required

sources.name: Accuracy-audit responsibility boundary
verified_claims: Home Office QA cannot determine whether the right crime was recorded
record-level accuracy requires audit of crime records
HMICFRS performs that audit function
limitations: administrative validation and accuracy audit are different
inspection intervals create information gaps
